content: Treatment with oseltamivir (TAMIFLU) should be initiated within 48 hours of the onset of influenza symptoms or following close contact with an individual infected with influenza. TAMIFLU can be taken with or without food; however, taking it with food may improve tolerability in some patients. For patients who are unable to swallow capsules, the preferred formulation is TAMIFLU oral suspension. If the oral suspension is unavailable, TAMIFLU capsules can be opened and mixed with sweetened liquids such as regular or sugar-free chocolate syrup, corn syrup, caramel topping, or light brown sugar dissolved in water. If neither the appropriate strength of capsules nor the oral suspension is available, a pharmacist may prepare an emergency supply of oral suspension using TAMIFLU 75 mg capsules. For the treatment of influenza in adults and adolescents aged 13 years and older, the recommended oral dose of TAMIFLU is 75 mg twice daily for 5 days. Each 5 mL of TAMIFLU oral suspension delivers 75 mg of the active ingredient. For pediatric patients aged 1 year to 12 years, the recommended oral dose of TAMIFLU for the treatment of influenza is based on body weight, as detailed in dosing guidelines. For pediatric patients aged 2 weeks to less than 1 year, the recommended dose is 3 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days. For the prophylaxis of influenza in adults and adolescents aged 13 years and older following close contact with an infected individual, the recommended oral dose of TAMIFLU is 75 mg once daily for at least 10 days. During a community outbreak of influenza, the recommended prophylactic dose is also 75 mg once daily. Safety and efficacy for prophylaxis have been demonstrated for up to 6 weeks in immunocompetent patients, with protection lasting as long as dosing continues. In immunocompromised patients, safety has been demonstrated for up to 12 weeks. Each 5 mL of TAMIFLU oral suspension delivers 75 mg of the active ingredient. For pediatric patients aged 1 to 12 years, the recommended oral dose of TAMIFLU for prophylaxis is based on body weight, as outlined in dosing guidelines. Prophylaxis following close contact with an infected individual is recommended for 10 days. During a community outbreak of influenza, prophylactic dosing in pediatric patients may be continued for up to 6 weeks.
